items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: Bob was a character, really character, you know. We'd -- let the reed section run off our parts

ctx.x: And he was very talented arranger, you know. So he would write parts like for the reeds, brass, like baritone, sax, bass and trombone, he would -- you know, he had that thing (unintelligible) with him. So we would

rehearse, were rehearsing. Bob was a character, really character, you know. We'd -- let the reed section run off our parts, and everything Jesse said (unintelligible) fine, and beautiful. So we'd lay the horns down. There's something wrong, some passages there, that bass and baritone sax and the trombones, he had a part played from the passages. So Bob was comical anyway, Bob. I said, what do you say, Bob? He said, huh, man, we've been here a whole three hours playing, practicing, rehearsing, and that cutback…

So Bob started to talk, said, I'm going to straighten that son of a bitch out. I said, Bob, leave the man alone. Well, (unintelligible) came back, he said, fellows, we going to learn this (unintelligible) again. So Bob said, hey, Jesse, -- what do you want to do now? He said, same thing. Well, the saxophone section, we got ours, said, what's wrong with that passage (unintelligible), said, everybody playing it but the trombones and the baritone and the trombone, but the bass player ain't reading that. That started…
